commands.name: New-OfficeMarkdown
commands.synopsis: Creates a Markdown file, optionally from a content block of Markdown DSL commands.
commands.notes: Content set: -Path is required, the block runs and the file is saved (FileInfo with -PassThru). Live set: no block, -Path optional; returns the live MarkdownDocument for Save-OfficeMarkdown [-Path]. Refuses an existing file unless -Force. Markdown has no theme, so no -Theme.

examples.title: Create a Markdown file
examples.description: Writes a heading and a paragraph to a new file and saves it when the block ends.

examples.title: Publish a stopped-services report
examples.description: Builds a report with front matter, a summary and a table from Get-Service, replacing yesterday's file.

examples.title: Keep the document open and save it later
examples.description: Without a content block the live document is returned, so a script can add to it in steps and choose the file name at the end.

commands.name: Open-OfficeMarkdown
commands.synopsis: Opens a Markdown file or parses Markdown text into a MarkdownDocument, optionally editing it in a content block.
commands.notes: Path/LiteralPath with a content block saves back to the file when the block ends. The Text set only parses and returns the document (no file to save). Reader settings (dialect profile, URL policy, input limits, normalization) come from New-OfficeMarkdownReaderOptions in -Options; they are no longer repeated as parameters. -Options takes New-OfficeMarkdownReaderOptions.

examples.title: Open a Markdown file
examples.description: Parses README.md into a MarkdownDocument for reading or editing.

examples.title: Append a release to the changelog
examples.description: Opens CHANGELOG.md, adds a new section at the end and saves the file back when the block ends.

examples.title: Parse Markdown returned by an API
examples.description: Parses Markdown text without a file and lists its section headings.

commands.name: Save-OfficeMarkdown
commands.synopsis: Saves a MarkdownDocument to its original path or to a new path.
commands.notes: -Path is optional; without it the document is saved to the path it was created or opened with. -PassThru returns the FileInfo.

examples.title: Save a document to its own file
examples.description: Writes the document back to the path it was opened or created with.

examples.title: Publish a copy with Windows line endings
examples.description: Opens the source README and saves a CRLF copy into the publish folder, returning the new file.

commands.name: Close-OfficeMarkdown
commands.synopsis: Releases a MarkdownDocument opened without a content block, without saving.
commands.notes: Lifecycle parity with every authoring format. MarkdownDocument holds no file handle, so this only ends the document's DSL scope.

examples.title: Release a document without saving
examples.description: Ends the document's scope; nothing is written.

examples.title: Inspect a runbook and discard it
examples.description: Opens a runbook, lists its top-level sections and closes it without writing changes.
examples.code:
$doc = Open-OfficeMarkdown -Path .\Docs\Runbook.md
Get-OfficeMarkdownHeading -Document $doc -MaxLevel 2 | Select-Object Level, Text
Close-OfficeMarkdown -Document $doc

commands.name: New-OfficeMarkdownPdfOptions
commands.synopsis: Creates Markdown-to-PDF options for Convert-OfficeDocument -To Pdf.
commands.notes: Defaults that are on (default theme, base-directory image restriction, front-matter theme and metadata, first heading as title, outline) are turned off with -No switches. IncludeLocalImages/IncludeDataUriImages stay opt-in resource-policy switches. -BaseOptions (or a piped options object) is copied and adjusted; it is named BaseOptions because -Options is the routed object[] list on the commands these options serve.

Convert-OfficeDocument -Path .\Runbooks\*.md -To Pdf -OutputDirectory .\Runbooks\Pdf -Options $pdf

commands.name: New-OfficeMarkdownPowerPointOptions
commands.synopsis: Creates Markdown-to-PowerPoint settings (slide breaks, title headings, speaker notes, images) for Convert-OfficeDocument -To PowerPoint.

parameters.name: SlideBreak
parameters.note: Where a new slide starts: ThematicBreakOrHeading (default: a --- line or a heading at -TitleHeadingLevel), ThematicBreak (--- lines only) or Heading (headings only).

parameters.name: TitleHeadingLevel
parameters.note: Heading level (1-6, default 1) that becomes the slide title and, with Heading breaks, starts a slide. Deeper headings stay as slide content.

parameters.name: NoBlockquoteNotes
parameters.note: Keep blockquotes on the slide as quotes; by default they become the speaker notes of their slide.

parameters.name: NoFrontMatter
parameters.note: Ignore YAML front matter; by default its title, subtitle and author fill the first slide.

parameters.name: BaseDirectory
parameters.note: Folder for relative image paths; default: the folder of the Markdown file.

parameters.name: NoMermaidDiagrams
parameters.note: Keep Mermaid blocks as code instead of rendering them as diagrams.

examples.title: Start slides only at --- lines
examples.description: Keeps headings inside a section on the same slide; a new slide starts only at a thematic break.

examples.title: Turn a folder of runbooks into themed decks
examples.description: Each level-2 heading becomes a slide title, local images are read from one folder and every deck uses the Boardroom theme from Convert-OfficeDocument -Theme.
examples.code:
$deck = New-OfficeMarkdownPowerPointOptions -SlideBreak Heading -TitleHeadingLevel 2 -AllowLocalImages -AllowedImageDirectory .\docs\images
Get-ChildItem -Path .\docs -Filter *.md |
    Convert-OfficeDocument -To PowerPoint -OutputDirectory .\Decks -Theme Boardroom -Options $deck

commands.notes: Used by Convert-OfficeDocument -To PowerPoint for Markdown sources. -Theme is not repeated here: Convert-OfficeDocument -Theme styles the new deck. Blockquotes become speaker notes and front matter fills the first slide by default; -NoBlockquoteNotes and -NoFrontMatter turn them off. Image and reader settings use the names of New-OfficeMarkdownWordOptions. New enum MarkdownSlideBreak: ThematicBreakOrHeading, ThematicBreak, Heading. MarkdownToPowerPointOptions is a new options type for the Markdown-to-PowerPoint route; OfficeIMO Markup keeps its own MarkupToPowerPointOptions.

examples.description: Shows one object as a two-column property table with -View Transpose, then the disks as a normal table.
examples.code:
$os = Get-CimInstance -ClassName Win32_OperatingSystem | Select-Object Caption, Version, LastBootUpTime
$disks = Get-CimInstance -ClassName Win32_LogicalDisk -Filter 'DriveType = 3' | Select-Object DeviceID, Size, FreeSpace

    MarkdownHeading $env:COMPUTERNAME

    MarkdownHeading 'Disks' -Level 2

}

commands.notes: DSL content command: inside New-/Open-OfficeMarkdown it writes to the enclosing document; the Document set appends to a document passed explicitly or from the pipeline. -PassThru returns the document. commands.name: New-OfficeRtf
commands.synopsis: Creates an RTF document, optionally with paragraphs from -Text or the pipeline.
commands.notes: -Text (or piped strings) writes one paragraph per string: in the Text set -Path is required and the file is written when input ends. The Live set (no -Text, -Path optional) returns the live RtfDocument; fill it with Add-OfficeRtfParagraph -Document and save it with Save-OfficeRtf [-Path] (replaces -NoSave).
